questions.prompt:
Bag A contains 6 red, 3 yellow and 3 green beads. Bag B only contains red and yellow beads.
A bead is selected at random from bag A and a second bead is selected at random from bag B.
Given that the probability that both beads selected are yellow is $\frac{1}{10}$
(a) (i) find the probability of selecting a yellow bead from bag B (2)
(ii) Hence find the probability on each branch of a tree diagram showing these selections (bag A first, then bag B). (2)
(b) Find the exact probability that at least one of the two beads selected is yellow. (3)
The event $X$ is that at least one of the beads selected is yellow. The event $W$ is that a green bead is selected.
(c) Find the exact value of $P(W \mid X)$ (2)
hints: (a) P(both yellow) = P(yellow from A) × P(yellow from B).
(b) Use 1 − P(no yellow at all).
(c) $P(W \mid X) = \frac{P(W \cap X)}{P(X)}$. If the green bead is chosen from A, X needs a yellow from B.
questions.solution:
(a)(i) $P(Y_A) = \frac{1}{4}$, so $\frac{1}{4} \times p = \frac{1}{10}$ [M1]
$p = \frac{2}{5}$ [A1]
(ii) Bag A: red $\frac{1}{2}$, yellow $\frac{1}{4}$, green $\frac{1}{4}$ [B1]
Bag B (on every branch): red $\frac{3}{5}$, yellow $\frac{2}{5}$ [B1]

(b) $P(\text{no yellow}) = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{3}{5} = \frac{9}{20}$ [M1]
$1 - \frac{9}{20}$ [M1]
$= \frac{11}{20}$ [A1]

(c) $P(W \cap X) = \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{10}$ [M1]
$P(W \mid X) = \frac{\frac{1}{10}}{\frac{11}{20}} = \frac{2}{11}$ [A1]

(a) State any pair of mutually exclusive events from $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ (1)
The events $B$ and $C$ are independent.
(b) Find the value of $p$ (2)
(c) Find the greatest possible value of $P(A \mid B')$ (3)
Given that $P(B \mid A') = 0.3$

(e) Find $P([A \cup B]' \cap C)$ (1)
(f) Use set notation to write an expression for the event with probability $p$ (1)

(c) $P(A \mid B') = \frac{q}{P(B')}$; $q$ is largest when $r = 0$.
(d) $P(B \mid A') = \frac{P(B \cap A')}{P(A')}$

questions.prompt:
A company has 1600 employees. The employees are classified as professional, skilled or elementary. The table shows the number of employees in each classification and the two areas, $A$ or $B$, where the employees live.
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|}\hline & A & B \\ \hline \text{Professional} & 600 & 300 \\ \hline \text{Skilled} & 240 & 160 \\ \hline \text{Elementary} & 200 & 100 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
An employee is chosen at random. Find the probability that this employee
(a) is skilled, (1)
(b) lives in area $B$ and is not a professional. (1)
Some classifications of employees are more likely to work from home: • 70% of professional employees in both area $A$ and area $B$ work from home • 30% of skilled employees in both areas work from home • 10% of elementary employees in both areas work from home. Event $F$ is that the employee is a professional, event $H$ is that the employee works from home and event $R$ is that the employee is from area $A$.
(c) Find the number of employees in each of these regions of a Venn diagram for $F$, $H$ and $R$: (i) $F \cap H \cap R$ (ii) $F \cap R \cap H'$ (iii) $H \cap F' \cap R'$ (iv) outside all three events (4)
(d) Find $P(R' \cap F)$ (1)
(e) Find $P([H \cup R]')$ (1)
(f) Find $P(F \mid H)$ (2)
hints: (c) For example, (iii) is employees in area $B$ who are not professionals but work from home.
(e) $[H \cup R]'$ is employees in area $B$ who don't work from home.
(f) $P(F \mid H) = \frac{P(F \cap H)}{P(H)}$

questions.prompt:
Athletes in a club can train with either coach A or coach B for the 400 m.
Coach A trains 100 athletes and records the best time, $x$ seconds, for each athlete. The results are summarised by
$$\sum x = 5530 \qquad \sum x^2 = 306250$$
(a) Calculate the mean of the best times for the athletes trained by coach A (1)
(b) Calculate the standard deviation of the best times for the athletes trained by coach A (2)
The mean and standard deviation for the best times of the athletes trained by coach B are 55.3 seconds and 3.4 seconds respectively.
A race consists of equal numbers of the fastest athletes trained by coach A and by coach B.
(c) State, giving a reason, which coach is more likely to have trained the winner. (2)
hints: Mean = Σx ÷ n.
Standard deviation = √(Σx²/n − mean²).
Compare both the averages and the spreads. Lower times are better.
questions.solution:
(a) $\bar{x} = \frac{5530}{100} = 55.3$ seconds [B1]

(b) $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{306250}{100} - 55.3^2}$ [M1]
$= 2.1$ seconds [A1]

(c) Coach B [B1]
because the means are the same, but coach B's times are more spread out (s.d. 3.4 compared with 2.1), so coach B's fastest runners are likely to be faster. [B1]

Coach A trains 150 athletes and records the best time, $x$ seconds, for each athlete. The results are summarised by
$$\sum x = 1860 \qquad \sum x^2 = 23118$$
(a) Calculate the mean of the best times for the athletes trained by coach A (1)
(b) Calculate the standard deviation of the best times for the athletes trained by coach A (2)

(c) State, giving a reason, which coach is more likely to have trained the winner. (2)

Standard deviation = √(Σx²/n − mean²).

questions.solution:

(b) $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{23118}{150} - 12.4^2}$ [M1]
$= 0.6$ seconds [A1]

(c) Coach A [B1]
because the standard deviations are the same, but coach A's mean time is lower, so coach A's runners are faster on average. [B1]

questions.prompt:
Kay is studying the variables Daily Mean Temperature ($x$ °C) and Daily Total Sunshine ($y$ hours) from the large data set for Camborne in 1987.
Kay starts with 3rd May and then selects every 7th day thereafter.
(a) State the name of the sampling technique Kay uses. (1)
Kay wants to find the regression line of $y$ on $x$ for these data.
(b) Using your knowledge of the large data set, explain how Kay might need to clean these data before finding the equation of the regression line. (1)
The equation of the regression line Kay finds is $y = -2.95 + 0.62x$
(c) Using your knowledge of the large data set, (i) state the units of the gradient of the regression line, (ii) give an interpretation of the $y$-intercept of the regression line. (2)
Kay's teacher claimed "the warmer the day, the more sunshine there should be".
(d) State, giving a reason, whether the teacher's claim is supported by Kay's data. (1)
The teacher used all the data for these variables from the large data set for Camborne in 1987, as a sample, and calculated the product moment correlation coefficient for $x$ and $y$ to be $0.284$. In a suitable test to determine whether there is evidence to support the teacher's claim, the $p$-value was $0.008$
(e) Using a 5% level of significance, state the hypotheses and conclusion for this test. (2)
(f) For the test in part (e) describe (i) the sample, (ii) a possible population. (2)
hints: Picking every $k$th item after a starting point is a named sampling method.
The large data set has 'n/a' entries (and 'tr' for trace rainfall).
The claim is one-directional, so the test is one-tailed.
questions.solution:
(a) (Quasi-)systematic sampling [B1]

(b) Remove any days with missing (n/a) values for either variable before finding the line. [B1]

(c)(i) hours per °C [B1]
(ii) $y$-intercept: the predicted sunshine on a day when the daily mean temperature is 0 °C (which is outside the data, so not meaningful) [B1]

(d) The gradient is positive, so Kay's data support the claim. [B1]

(e) $H_0: \rho = 0$, $H_1: \rho > 0$ [B1]
$p$-value $0.008 < 0.05$: reject $H_0$; there is sufficient evidence to support the teacher's claim. [B1]

(f)(i) The sample: the days from 1st May to 31st October 1987 at Camborne (the data in the large data set) [B1]
(ii) A possible population: all days from May to October at Camborne (in any year) [B1]

questions.prompt:
Amar is studying the flight of a bird from its nest. He measures its height above the ground, $h$ metres, at time $t$ seconds for 10 values of $t$.
Amar finds the equation of the regression line for the data to be $h = 41.4 - 1.65t$
(a) Interpret the gradient of this line. (1)
The product moment correlation coefficient between $h$ and $t$ is $-0.698$
(b) Test whether or not there is evidence of a negative correlation between the height above the ground and the time during the flight. You should • state your hypotheses clearly • use a 5% level of significance • state the critical value used (3)
Jane draws the scatter diagram shown for Amar's data.
(c) With reference to the scatter diagram, state, giving a reason, whether or not the regression line $h = 41.4 - 1.65t$ is an appropriate model for these data. (1)
Jane suggests an improved model using the variable $u = (t - k)^2$, where $k$ is a constant. She obtains the equation $h = 39.8 - 0.90u$
(d) Choose a suitable value for $k$ to write Jane's improved model for $h$ in terms of $t$ only. (1)
hints: (a) The gradient is the change in $h$ per second.
(b) One-tailed test: $H_1: \rho < 0$. The critical value for $n = 10$ at 5% is in the formula book's table.
(d) In $c - d(t - k)^2$, the maximum is at $t = k$. Where does the scatter diagram peak?
questions.solution:
(a) The height of the bird decreases by about 1.65 m each second. [B1]

(b) $H_0: \rho = 0$, $H_1: \rho < 0$ [B1]
Critical value $-0.5494$ [M1]
$-0.698 < -0.5494$, so reject $H_0$: there is sufficient evidence of a negative correlation. [A1]

(c) Not appropriate: the points follow a curve (the height rises then falls), not a straight line. [B1]

(d) The peak is at about $t = 3.5$, so $k = 3.5$: $h = 39.8 - 0.90(t - 3.5)^2$ [B1]

questions.prompt:
Amar is studying the flight of a kite. He measures its height above the ground, $h$ metres, at time $t$ seconds for 11 values of $t$.
Amar finds the equation of the regression line for the data to be $h = 34.0 - 2.23t$
(a) Interpret the gradient of this line. (1)
The product moment correlation coefficient between $h$ and $t$ is $-0.739$
(b) Test whether or not there is evidence of a negative correlation between the height above the ground and the time during the flight. You should • state your hypotheses clearly • use a 5% level of significance • state the critical value used (3)
Jane draws the scatter diagram shown for Amar's data.
(c) With reference to the scatter diagram, state, giving a reason, whether or not the regression line $h = 34.0 - 2.23t$ is an appropriate model for these data. (1)
Jane suggests an improved model using the variable $u = (t - k)^2$, where $k$ is a constant. She obtains the equation $h = 32.0 - 1.14u$
(d) Choose a suitable value for $k$ to write Jane's improved model for $h$ in terms of $t$ only. (1)
hints: (a) The gradient is the change in $h$ per second.
(b) One-tailed test: $H_1: \rho < 0$. The critical value for $n = 11$ at 5% is in the formula book's table.
(d) In $c - d(t - k)^2$, the maximum is at $t = k$. Where does the scatter diagram peak?
questions.solution:
(a) The height of the kite decreases by about 2.23 m each second. [B1]

(b) $H_0: \rho = 0$, $H_1: \rho < 0$ [B1]
Critical value $-0.5214$ [M1]
$-0.739 < -0.5214$, so reject $H_0$: there is sufficient evidence of a negative correlation. [A1]

(c) Not appropriate: the points follow a curve (the height rises then falls), not a straight line. [B1]

(d) The peak is at about $t = 3$, so $k = 3$: $h = 32.0 - 1.14(t - 3)^2$ [B1]

questions.prompt:
Amar is studying the flight of a drone. He measures its height above the ground, $h$ metres, at time $t$ seconds for 12 values of $t$.
Amar finds the equation of the regression line for the data to be $h = 42.4 - 0.72t$
(a) Interpret the gradient of this line. (1)
The product moment correlation coefficient between $h$ and $t$ is $-0.414$
(b) Test whether or not there is evidence of a negative correlation between the height above the ground and the time during the flight. You should • state your hypotheses clearly • use a 5% level of significance • state the critical value used (3)
Jane draws the scatter diagram shown for Amar's data.
(c) With reference to the scatter diagram, state, giving a reason, whether or not the regression line $h = 42.4 - 0.72t$ is an appropriate model for these data. (1)
Jane suggests an improved model using the variable $u = (t - k)^2$, where $k$ is a constant. She obtains the equation $h = 43.4 - 0.83u$
(d) Choose a suitable value for $k$ to write Jane's improved model for $h$ in terms of $t$ only. (1)
hints: (a) The gradient is the change in $h$ per second.
(b) One-tailed test: $H_1: \rho < 0$. The critical value for $n = 12$ at 5% is in the formula book's table.
(d) In $c - d(t - k)^2$, the maximum is at $t = k$. Where does the scatter diagram peak?
questions.solution:
(a) The height of the drone decreases by about 0.72 m each second. [B1]

(b) $H_0: \rho = 0$, $H_1: \rho < 0$ [B1]
Critical value $-0.4973$ [M1]
$-0.414 > -0.4973$, so do not reject $H_0$: there is insufficient evidence of a negative correlation. [A1]

(c) Not appropriate: the points follow a curve (the height rises then falls), not a straight line. [B1]

(d) The peak is at about $t = 4$, so $k = 4$: $h = 43.4 - 0.83(t - 4)^2$ [B1]

hints: (a) Which variable in the large data set has values of this size?
(b) $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2}$
(c) Think about the season at that location from May to October.
questions.solution:
(a) Daily Mean Pressure (hPa) [B1]

(b) $\bar{x} = \frac{2208}{184} = 12.00$ °C [B1]

questions.prompt:
A medical researcher is studying the number of hours, $T$, a patient stays in hospital following a particular operation. The histogram summarises the results for a random sample of 120 patients.
(a) Use the histogram to estimate $P(5 < T < 25)$ (2)
For these 120 patients the time spent in hospital had • a mean of 14.6 hours • a standard deviation of 9.2 hours. Tomas suggests that $T$ can be modelled by $N(14.6, 9.2^2)$
(b) With reference to the histogram, state, giving a reason, whether or not Tomas' model could be suitable. (1)
Xiang suggests that the frequency polygon based on this histogram could be modelled by a curve with equation $$y = kxe^{-x} \qquad 0 \leqslant x \leqslant 4$$ where • $x$ is measured in tens of hours • $k$ is a constant.
(c) Use algebraic integration to show that $$\int_0^n xe^{-x}\,dx = 1 - (n + 1)e^{-n}$$ (4)
(d) Show that, for Xiang's model, $k = 132$ to the nearest integer. (3)
(e) Estimate $P(5 < T < 25)$ using
(i) Tomas' model of $T \sim N(14.6, 9.2^2)$ (1)
(ii) Xiang's curve with equation $y = 132xe^{-x}$ and the answer to part (c) (2)
The researcher decides to use Xiang's curve to model $P(a < T < b)$.
(f) State one limitation of Xiang's model. (1)
hints: (a) Frequency = frequency density × class width. You may need part of a bar.
(c) Integrate by parts with $u = x$.
(d) The total area under the curve (with $x$ from 0 to 4) should equal the total frequency, 120.
(e)(ii) Convert hours to tens of hours: $x$ goes from 0.5 to 2.5.
questions.solution:
(a) Frequency between 5 and 25 hours $\approx 85.125$ [M1]
$P \approx \frac{85.125}{120} = 0.709$ [A1]

(b) Not suitable: the histogram is not symmetrical (it is positively skewed), and $N(14.6, 9.2^2)$ would give a probability of 0.056 of a negative time. [B1]

(c) By parts, $u = x$, $\frac{dv}{dx} = e^{-x}$: $\int xe^{-x}\,dx = -xe^{-x} + \int e^{-x}\,dx$ [M1 A1]
$= -xe^{-x} - e^{-x}$ [A1]
$\left[-(x + 1)e^{-x}\right]_0^n = 1 - (n + 1)e^{-n}$ [A1]

(d) Total area $= 120$: $k\int_0^4 xe^{-x}\,dx = 120$ [M1]
$k(1 - 5e^{-4}) = 120$ [M1]
$k = 132.10$, so $k = 132$ to the nearest integer [A1]

(e)(i) $0.7225$ [B1]
(ii) $\frac{132}{120}\left[\left(1 - 3.5e^{-2.5}\right) - \left(1 - 1.5e^{-0.5}\right)\right]$ [M1]
$= 0.6847$ [A1]

(f) For example: the curve only covers up to 40 hours, so it can't model patients staying longer; or the frequency polygon is only an approximation to the data. [B1]

(a) Write down how a value of $0 < r \leqslant 0.05$ is recorded in the large data set. (1)
Dian uses the data for the 31 days of July 1987 for Hurn and calculates the following statistics $$n = 31 \qquad \sum r = 58.9 \qquad \sum r^2 = 742.15$$
(b) Use these statistics to calculate (i) the mean Daily Total Rainfall for Hurn for July 1987, (ii) the standard deviation of the Daily Total Rainfall for Hurn for July 1987. (3)
Dian believes that the mean Daily Total Rainfall in July is less in the South of the UK than in the North. The mean Daily Total Rainfall in Leuchars for July 1987 is 2.31 mm to 2 decimal places.
(c) State, giving a reason, whether this provides evidence to support Dian's belief. (2)
Dian uses the large data set to estimate the proportion of days with no rain in Hurn for 1987 to be 0.27 to 2 decimal places.
(d) Explain why the distribution $B(14, 0.27)$ might not be a reasonable model for the number of days without rain for a 14-day summer event. (1)
hints: (b) $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum r^2}{n} - \bar{r}^2}$
(d) Think about whether dry days happen independently of each other.

but it is only one month, one year and two locations, so it is weak evidence. [B1]

(d) Dry days are not independent (dry weather tends to come in spells), or the probability of a dry day is not constant across the summer. [B1]

(a) Write down how a value of $0 < r \leqslant 0.05$ is recorded in the large data set. (1)
Dian uses the data for the 30 days of September 1987 for Camborne and calculates the following statistics $$n = 30 \qquad \sum r = 102.6 \qquad \sum r^2 = 1450.4$$
(b) Use these statistics to calculate (i) the mean Daily Total Rainfall for Camborne for September 1987, (ii) the standard deviation of the Daily Total Rainfall for Camborne for September 1987. (3)
Dian believes that the mean Daily Total Rainfall in September is greater in the South-West of the UK than in the South-East. The mean Daily Total Rainfall in Heathrow for September 1987 is 1.95 mm to 2 decimal places.
(c) State, giving a reason, whether this provides evidence to support Dian's belief. (2)
Dian uses the large data set to estimate the proportion of days with no rain in Camborne for 1987 to be 0.27 to 2 decimal places.
(d) Explain why the distribution $B(14, 0.27)$ might not be a reasonable model for the number of days without rain for a 14-day summer event. (1)
hints: (b) $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum r^2}{n} - \bar{r}^2}$
(d) Think about whether dry days happen independently of each other.
questions.solution:
(a) It is recorded as 'tr' (trace). [B1]

(b)(i) $\bar{r} = \frac{102.6}{30} = 3.420$ mm [B1]
(ii) $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{1450.4}{30} - 3.420^2}$ [M1]
$= 6.054$ mm [A1]

(c) Camborne's mean (3.42 mm) is greater than Heathrow's (1.95 mm), so this supports Dian's belief [B1]
but it is only one month, one year and two locations, so it is weak evidence. [B1]

(d) Dry days are not independent (dry weather tends to come in spells), or the probability of a dry day is not constant across the summer. [B1]

questions.prompt:
Anna is investigating the relationship between exercise and resting heart rate. She takes a random sample of 15 people in her year at school and records for each person • their resting heart rate, $h$ beats per minute • the number of minutes, $m$, spent exercising each week. Her results are shown on the scatter diagram.
(a) Interpret the nature of the relationship between $h$ and $m$ (1)
Anna codes the data using $x = \log_{10} m$ and $y = \log_{10} h$. The product moment correlation coefficient between $x$ and $y$ is $-0.988$
(b) Test whether or not there is significant evidence of a negative correlation between $x$ and $y$. You should • state your hypotheses clearly • use a 5% level of significance • state the critical value used (3)
The equation of the line of best fit of $y$ on $x$ is $y = -0.090x + 1.963$
(c) Use the equation of the line of best fit of $y$ on $x$ to find a model for $h$ on $m$ in the form $h = am^k$, where $a$ and $k$ are constants to be found. (5)
hints: (b) One-tailed test, $H_1: \rho < 0$; use the critical value for $n = 15$.
(c) Write $\log_{10} h = k\log_{10} m + c$, then raise 10 to the power of both sides.
questions.solution:
(a) As the minutes of exercise increase, resting heart rate decreases, but not linearly (it levels off). [B1]

(b) $H_0: \rho = 0$, $H_1: \rho < 0$ [B1]
Critical value $-0.4409$ [M1]
$-0.988 < -0.4409$: reject $H_0$; there is sufficient evidence of a negative correlation between $x$ and $y$. [A1]

(c) $\log_{10} h = -0.090\log_{10} m + 1.963$ [M1]
$h = 10^{1.963} \times 10^{-0.090\log_{10} m}$ [M1]
$= 10^{1.963} m^{-0.090}$ [M1 A1]
$a = 91.8$, $k = -0.090$ [A1]

She takes a random sample of 20 people in her year at school and records for each person • their resting heart rate, $h$ beats per minute • the number of minutes, $m$, spent exercising each week. Her results are shown on the scatter diagram.

(c) Use the equation of the line of best fit of $y$ on $x$ to find a model for $h$ on $m$ in the form $h = am^k$, where $a$ and $k$ are constants to be found. (5)

(b) $H_0: \rho = 0$, $H_1: \rho < 0$ [B1]

questions.prompt:
Anna is investigating the relationship between exercise and resting heart rate. She takes a random sample of 12 people in her year at school and records for each person • their resting heart rate, $h$ beats per minute • the number of minutes, $m$, spent exercising each week. Her results are shown on the scatter diagram.
(a) Interpret the nature of the relationship between $h$ and $m$ (1)
Anna codes the data using $x = \log_{10} m$ and $y = \log_{10} h$. The product moment correlation coefficient between $x$ and $y$ is $-0.940$
(b) Test whether or not there is significant evidence of a negative correlation between $x$ and $y$. You should • state your hypotheses clearly • use a 5% level of significance • state the critical value used (3)
The equation of the line of best fit of $y$ on $x$ is $y = -0.058x + 1.934$
(c) Use the equation of the line of best fit of $y$ on $x$ to find a model for $h$ on $m$ in the form $h = am^k$, where $a$ and $k$ are constants to be found. (5)
hints: (b) One-tailed test, $H_1: \rho < 0$; use the critical value for $n = 12$.
(c) Write $\log_{10} h = k\log_{10} m + c$, then raise 10 to the power of both sides.
questions.solution:
(a) As the minutes of exercise increase, resting heart rate decreases, but not linearly (it levels off). [B1]

(b) $H_0: \rho = 0$, $H_1: \rho < 0$ [B1]
Critical value $-0.4973$ [M1]
$-0.940 < -0.4973$: reject $H_0$; there is sufficient evidence of a negative correlation between $x$ and $y$. [A1]

(c) $\log_{10} h = -0.058\log_{10} m + 1.934$ [M1]
$h = 10^{1.934} \times 10^{-0.058\log_{10} m}$ [M1]
$= 10^{1.934} m^{-0.058}$ [M1 A1]
$a = 85.9$, $k = -0.058$ [A1]

questions.prompt:
The discrete random variable $R$ takes odd integer values from 1 to $2n - 1$ inclusive. The probability distribution of $R$ is given by
$$P(R = r) = \frac{r}{k} \qquad r = 1, 3, 5, \ldots, 2n - 1$$
where $k$ is a constant.
(a) Show that $k = n^2$ (4)
When $n = 10$
(b) find the exact value of $P(5 \leqslant R < 12)$ (2)
When $n = 10$, a random value $g$ of $R$ is taken and the quadratic equation in $x$ $$x^2 + gx + 2g = 3$$ is formed.
(c) Find the exact probability that the equation has no real roots. (5)
hints: (a) The probabilities add up to 1, so $k$ = the sum of all the values of $r$.
(c) No real roots means $b^2 - 4ac < 0$.
questions.solution:
(a) $\sum P(R = r) = 1 \Rightarrow k = $ sum of the values [M1]
The values form an arithmetic series with $n$ terms [M1]
Sum $= \frac{n}{2}(\text{first} + \text{last})$ [M1]
$k = n^2$ [A1]

(b) $k = 100$; $P = \frac{5 + 7 + 9 + 11}{100}$ [M1]
$= \frac{8}{25}$ [A1]

(c) Rearrange: $x^2 + gx + (2g - 3) = 0$ [M1]
No real roots: $g^{2} - 8 g + 12 < 0$ [M1]
Critical values $g = 2$ and $g = 6$, so $2 < g < 6$ [A1]
Possible values of $g$: 3, 5 [M1]
$P = \frac{3 + 5}{100} = \frac{2}{25}$ [A1]
